item.title: Wendy’s rejects billionaire Nelson Peltz’s $1.4 billion takeover bid, adopts ‘poison pill’ defence as burger chain shuts hundreds of US outlets
item.description: Wendy's has rejected a takeover proposal valued at $1.4 billion from billionaire investor Nelson Peltz. The fast-food chain argued that the offer undervalues its long-term growth potential, prompting the adoption of a shareholder rights plan. This defensive strategy is designed to protect the company from unwanted acquisition attempts. Wendy's has been facing declining sales and rising operational costs in the competitive fast-food market.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After years of flooding, Philippine village turns to bamboo, oyster shells and coconut waste to keep rising waters at bay
item.description: Pamarawan village in the Philippines has embraced an innovative coastal defense system to tackle flooding challenges. This initiative incorporates natural materials such as bamboo poles, oyster shells, and coconut husks to fortify against powerful waves and prevent sediment displacement. Remarkably, there have been no flooding incidents reported for almost two years since the project's inception, prompting officials to explore similar setups for other flood-threatened areas.

item.title: Another attack on Iran soon? Trump meets top security advisers after midterm elections
item.description: US President Donald Trump held meetings to evaluate potential military operations against Iran's nuclear program. item.title: Scientists examining dinosaur fossils report evidence of preserved red blood cells and collagen amino acids, a finding led by Curtin University that could change how researchers investigate ancient biological material
item.description: Palaeontologists found fossilised signs of dinosaur blood and collagen in a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone. These structures were discovered in a theropod dinosaur known as Aratasaurus museunacionali. Advanced techniques identified iron-containing heme and collagen, suggesting biological materials survived long periods. Researchers believe rapid burial in low-oxygen conditions contributed to preservation. This discovery opens new avenues for understanding dinosaur biology beyond skeletal remains.

item.title: Archaeologists studying an ancient Spanish copper mine uncovered stone tools and new evidence of Bronze Age production; the findings suggest metal from Iberia may have travelled as far north as Scandinavia
item.description: Archaeologists conducted a thorough investigation of Las Minillas, an ancient copper mine in southern Spain, revealing its historical impact. Over 700 stone tools and pottery shards were found, pinpointing extensive activity from 1300 to 700 BC. This research indicates that the copper mined here likely reached Scandinavia through trade networks, showcasing the interconnectedness of Bronze Age communities across Europe.

item.title: Trump team stands firm: Rubio rules out exit, Hegseth gets president's backing
item.description: Marco Rubio has dismissed rumors about potentially leaving his position in the Trump administration. He asserts that completing Trump's second term has always been his plan. While he supports Vice President JD Vance for a future presidential run, Rubio avoids discussing his ambitions. Reports regarding a possible exit have been rejected by the White House and the State Department.

item.title: 'Vote red today!' Elon Musk deletes pro-Republican posts after spending $458 million
item.description: Elon Musk removed social media posts encouraging support for Republican candidates after Democrats achieved significant victories. His pinned message included a call to vote Republican on Election Day. Musk’s financial backing totaled around $458 million, making him a significant donor during the election cycle. The election results also caused a decline in Musk's personal wealth and the stock values of his companies.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 'You'll know soon enough': Trump's warning on 'destroying' rest of Iran
item.description: During a press conference at the Oval Office, Donald Trump cautioned Iran regarding its nuclear ambitions, hinting at possible future actions while preferring to avoid escalation. He asserted that Iran must seek US approval for any developments in its nuclear program, showcasing America's ongoing influence. These statements highlight the escalating tensions and complex dynamics between the two nations.

item.title: Julia Child Home Sells: former Cambridge house fetches $6.525 million; kitchen lives on at Smithsonian
item.description: Julia Child’s iconic home in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has found a new owner for $6.525 million. This historic residence, adored for its connection to Child's culinary shows, has seen extensive renovations. The original kitchen, however, remains untouched and is now a cherished exhibit at the Smithsonian Museum. To honor her legacy, a commemorative plaque is set to be installed at the site, ensuring that Child's influence on cooking continues.

item.title: US wildlife teams surveyed six offshore islands for invasive species, finding rats on five and iguanas on one; the results will guide future work to protect nesting seabirds
item.description: Recent surveys in the U.S. Virgin Islands have identified invasive species on several offshore cays. Black rats and green iguanas pose significant threats to local seabird populations, such as the red-billed tropicbird. Conservationists are now evaluating strategies to eradicate these non-native animals from the islands. Removal efforts could lead to improved nesting conditions for seabirds in the future. Successful initiatives may help restore these vital habitats for future generations.
